papers.title: Temporal drift of sleep-wake representations in hypothalamic neuronal ensembles.
papers.summary: Using longitudinal single-cell calcium imaging in freely-moving mice, the study found that hypothalamic neurons (inhibitory, excitatory, hypocretin/orexin, melanin-concentrating hormone) show dynamic, state-dependent shifts in activity across sleep-wake states over time, rather than stable state-specific activity. Sleep deprivation minimally affected these activity patterns, while diazepam recruited NREM-active cells, suggesting population-level stability despite neuronal drift.

papers.title: Decoding Sleep Architecture from Ambulatory Basal Ganglia Signals in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study used chronic ambulatory subthalamic nucleus recordings from 18 Parkinson's disease patients (via BrainSense-enabled neurostimulators) with wearables to decode sleep architecture, showing distinct spectral biomarkers (low-frequency, beta, finely-tuned gamma) with circadian modulation across sleep stages. Machine learning classifiers decoded states (e.g., deep sleep identified by low-frequency activity), with implications for diagnostics and adaptive deep brain stimulation.

papers.title: Mathematical Modeling of Dietary Timing- and Protein Quality-Responsive Liver Circadian Clock and its Function on Ribosome Biogenesis.
papers.summary: Developed a semi-mechanistic mathematical model of liver circadian entrainment by feeding/fasting cycles and dietary essential amino acid (EAA) availability, integrating mTORC1 and GCN2-ISR signaling with ribosome biogenesis. The model predicted that these pathways jointly regulate metabolic entrainability and that modulating GCN2-ISR signaling can mitigate disruption-associated ribosomal biogenesis hyperactivation.

papers.title: Theta oscillations tag episodic memories for sleep-dependent consolidation.
papers.summary: Using multivariate EEG classification in humans, the study decoded brain states for episodic memories tagged at learning for consolidation across sleep or wakefulness, linking tagging across sleep to 3-8 Hz theta rhythms during learning. Theta magnitude predicted slow oscillation-spindle coupling during post-learning sleep, which in turn was associated with enhanced memory performance, providing evidence for a neural tagging mechanism.

papers.title: Around the Clock: Wearing a Flex-Printed trEEGrid Electrode Patch and Miniaturized Amplifier for Nearly 24 Hours Across Daytime and Overnight EEG Sessions.
papers.summary: This study validated a novel flex-printed trEEGrid electrode patch and miniaturized amplifier for long-term (up to 24 h) EEG recordings on 10 participants, including daytime tasks and overnight sleep. The system showed comparable signal quality to ring electrodes for auditory N1 amplitudes and captured P3, resting state, and workload-related spectral effects on both days, supporting its utility for extended monitoring.

papers.title: Slow-Wave Sleep Mediates the Compensatory Effects of Acute Moderate-Intensity Exercise on Declarative Memory Deficits in Sleep Restriction.
papers.summary: In a randomized study of 88 healthy young adults, a single session of evening moderate-intensity exercise before sleep restriction improved delayed recall of face-name pairs compared to no exercise, with performance comparable to normal sleep groups. Slow-wave sleep proportion statistically mediated the effect, suggesting exercise offsets sleep restriction-induced memory deficits via SWS enhancement.

papers.title: [Research on electrooculography artifact removal from electroencephalography signals based on frequency slice wavelet transform].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.summary: This paper proposes an improved frequency slice wavelet transform (FSWT) method for removing electrooculography (EOG) artifacts from single-channel EEG signals. The method achieved a mean signal-to-noise ratio improvement of 2.81 dB on all contaminated samples and 5.69 dB on strongly contaminated samples, while retaining theta-band energy at a rate of 0.889.

papers.title: Disentangling EEG Fingerprinting and Sleep Biomarkers Using Generalized Weighted Ordinal Patterns.
papers.summary: This study evaluates generalized weighted ordinal patterns (GWOP) for sleep stage classification and finds that they generalize well to unseen subjects (accuracy drop from 79.2% to 75.8% between intra- and inter-subject validation) while also preserving subject identity information (63.9% identification accuracy), indicating a partial separation between identity and biomarker information.

papers.title: Development and Explainable Machine Learning Validation of a Novel Sleep Disturbance Ratio for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severity Assessment.
papers.summary: This study introduces a novel polysomnography-derived biomarker, the Sleep Disturbance Ratio (SDR), and evaluates its contribution to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity classification using explainable machine learning. Random Forest achieved highest accuracy (75.0%), XGBoost achieved best multiclass AUC (0.895), and SDR provided complementary information particularly when combined with oxygenation parameters.

papers.title: From plate to pillow: the role of food-derived bioactive compounds in sleep modulation and the potential of glia-neuron crosstalk.
papers.summary: This review evaluates five major categories of food-derived bioactive compounds (amino acids, polyphenols, fatty acids, bioactive peptides, and melatonin/indole derivatives) for sleep modulation. It proposes a periphery-to-center axis involving gut microbiota, blood-brain barrier, and glia-neuron crosstalk, highlighting glial cells as active regulators of sleep homeostasis.

papers.title: Shared Spectral Parameters Between EEG and Basal Ganglia LFP Distinguish Sleep-Specific Oscillations in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: This study recorded simultaneous polysomnography and subthalamic nucleus local field potentials in 19 Parkinson's disease patients, finding that aperiodic spectral parameters (exponent and offset) differ between EEG and LFP across sleep stages and that STN-LFP aperiodic features alone classified sleep stages above chance. These findings suggest potential biomarkers for closed-loop neuromodulation targeting sleep dysfunction.

papers.title: Circadian Biology and Phase Response: Fundamental Mechanisms and Clinical Applications.
papers.summary: This review describes fundamental mechanisms of the circadian clock, including light and melatonin entrainment, phase response curves, and the adverse health effects of circadian disruption in shift workers. It also discusses clinical interventions to realign circadian rhythms and improve shift work adaptation.

papers.title: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Disrupts Intestinal Homeostasis Through Gut Microbiota Remodeling and Microbiota-Metabolite Interactions.
papers.summary: The study exposed mice to chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) and found disrupted colonic barrier integrity, gut microbial dysbiosis with depletion of Akkermansia muciniphila, and altered fecal/serum metabolomics, suggesting CIH disrupts intestinal homeostasis via coordinated microbiota-metabolite interactions.

papers.title: A preliminary investigation of the relationship between rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and fear inhibition processes in the context of circadian misalignment.
papers.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
papers.summary: In a randomized trial with 42 healthy adults, experimentally induced circadian misalignment predicted reduced REM sleep, and reductions in REM minutes predicted poorer extinction recall, suggesting circadian misalignment may impair fear inhibition via REM sleep loss.

papers.title: Non-Pharmacological Strategies in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Integration.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and clinical evidence on non-pharmacological strategies for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, covering dietary patterns, chrononutrition, microbiome modulation, and nutraceuticals, and highlights their synergistic effects with pharmacotherapy.

papers.title: LD-CNN19: A Deep Learning Model Integrating Logical Reasoning and Knowledge Expansion for Small-Sample Sleep Staging Tasks.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The study proposes LD-CNN19, a neuro-symbolic deep learning framework for sleep staging that integrates logical reasoning and adaptive knowledge expansion, improving macro F1-scores by up to 4.22% and enhancing decision stability in small-sample settings.

papers.title: Toward a Predictive Coding Account of Hypnotic Hypoalgesia: Integrating EEG Oscillations and Somatosensory Evoked Responses.
papers.summary: This review integrates EEG and somatosensory evoked potential evidence on hypnotic hypoalgesia, interpreting findings through predictive coding and active inference, and suggests hypnotic suggestions alter pain salience and appraisal rather than early sensory processing.

papers.title: SleepStageNet: A Lightweight and Explainable Deep Learning Architecture for Multi-Channel Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: This study presents SleepStageNet, a compact deep learning model for automatic sleep staging from five PSG channels, evaluated on an Indian stroke cohort (95 subjects) achieving 73.91% accuracy and κ=0.634. Ablation studies showed C4-only input significantly reduced performance, while a 10-model ensemble generalized to ISRUC-SLEEP with κ=0.614 without fine-tuning.

papers.title: Evaluating Validation Strategies in Motor Imagery EEG: A Full-Cohort GAF-PLV Analysis and Matched Sensitivity Study.
papers.summary: This study evaluated validation strategies for motor imagery EEG classification, showing that random cross-validation overestimates performance compared to leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. On a full cohort (N=105), GAF-PLV achieved 58.07% accuracy, and model rankings varied by validation strategy, highlighting the need for subject-independent evaluation.

papers.title: Developmental and/or Epileptic Encephalopathy with Spike-Wave Activation in Sleep: From Thalamocortical Mechanisms to Precision Therapy.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the pathophysiology, genetics, and treatment of developmental/epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep (D/EE-SWAS), highlighting its thalamocortical network basis and genomic heterogeneity. It notes that corticosteroids have the strongest evidence for cognitive improvement, though overall evidence is low to moderate, and emerging precision therapies target specific genetic etiologies.

papers.title: Automated Multimodal Sleep Staging Using DWT-Based Wavelet Decomposition and Explainable Machine Learning with Signal Sculpting Topographies.
papers.summary: This study developed an explainable machine learning framework for automated five-class sleep staging using EEG, EOG, and EMG signals from 30 healthy subjects, with SVM-RBF achieving 75.18% accuracy and macro F1 of 0.7322. SHAP analysis identified EMG RMS amplitude, gamma power, and permutation entropy as top discriminative features, and novel signal sculpting visualizations were introduced for clinical interpretability.

papers.title: Motor Sequence Learning Under Sleep Deprivation.
papers.summary: This study examined the effect of one night of total sleep deprivation on motor sequence learning in 48 healthy adults, finding that SD selectively reduced movement time gains but not spatial accuracy, with no effects on consolidation at 24h and 7 days. SD elevated cortisol and reduced vigilance but did not alter BDNF or corticospinal excitability.

papers.title: [Multi-view signal integration via manifold learning for sleep stage classification].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.summary: The paper proposes a multi-view spatio-temporal convolutional integration network based on manifold learning for sleep stage classification, integrating EEG and other physiological signals. It outperforms existing mainstream methods on public datasets in accuracy, F1-score, and Kappa coefficient.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Chronotype and Depression Among Adolescents: The Mediating Role of Bedtime Procrastination and the Moderating Role of Parental Psychological Control.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 4324 adolescents found that chronotype is negatively associated with depression, with bedtime procrastination mediating 55.75% of the effect and parental psychological control moderating the relationships. The findings suggest multilevel interventions targeting sleep hygiene and family dynamics may reduce depressive risk.

papers.title: The functional significance of EEG phase synchronization networks during information integration of left and right visual fields
papers.summary: This study used EEG and a visual integration task to identify a broadband phase synchronization network that emerges when integrating information across visual hemifields. Individual differences in task performance were related to modulation of interhemispheric synchronization, suggesting large-scale phase synchronization supports visual integration.

papers.title: qEEG and Functional Connectivity as a Translational Bridge Between Humans and Dogs in Epilepsy and Associated Disorders: From Spontaneous Model to Automatic Classification-An Integrative Review.
papers.summary: This integrative review of 75 studies examines quantitative EEG (qEEG) and functional connectivity in humans and dogs with epilepsy and related disorders, highlighting the dog as a natural translational model. It finds cross-species similarities in EEG alterations and supports qEEG as a promising biomarker, though standardized validation is needed.

papers.title: CLOCK 3111T/C Polymorphism and Sex Moderate the Effect of Childhood Trauma on White Matter Microstructure in Bipolar Disorder.
papers.summary: This study of 137 bipolar disorder patients found that the CLOCK 3111T/C polymorphism moderates the effect of childhood trauma on white matter microstructure, with female C allele carriers showing greater vulnerability. The effects were genotype-specific in females but not males.

papers.title: The Influence of Shared Attention and Friendship on Emotional Processing: A Behavioral and EEG Hyperscanning Study.
papers.summary: This EEG hyperscanning study with 39 dyads (friends vs strangers) examined how shared attention and friendship modulate emotional processing. Shared attention increased beta and theta inter-brain synchrony in the prefrontal cortex for friends but decreased synchrony for strangers, and alpha synchrony decreased with shared attention for consistent images, revealing band-specific neural mechanisms.

papers.title: Repeated Continuous Theta-Burst Stimulation Modulates Resting-State EEG Microstate Dynamics in Athletes with Chronic Insomnia.
papers.summary: In a randomized sham-controlled trial, 7 days of right dorsolateral prefrontal cTBS improved sleep quality and athletic performance in 32 male athletes with chronic insomnia. Resting-state EEG microstate dynamics changed, with increased microstate C and decreased microstate A, suggesting potential electrophysiological correlates of treatment response.

papers.title: Psychobiological Correlates of Instructed Deceptive Responding: An Exploratory EEG Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory EEG study with 86 adults found that instructed deceptive responding was associated with increased right-frontal theta power, and trait anxiety positively correlated with self-reported deceptive behavior. Findings suggest involvement of executive control and conflict monitoring mechanisms.

papers.title: Potential Contributions of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms to Behavioral Difficulties in Children with Smith-Magenis Syndrome in Real Life: An Actigraphy-Based Study.
papers.summary: This actigraphy-based cohort study of 20 children with Smith-Magenis syndrome found that subjective sleep disturbances correlated with irritability, stereotypic behavior, and inappropriate speech, while circadian rhythm parameters (earlier L5 onset) were associated with hyperactivity and social withdrawal, suggesting potential intervention targets.

papers.title: Objective Sleep Architecture Alterations and Sleep-Dependent Brain Clearance Dysfunction Across the Early Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review (4 studies) assessed the relationship between objectively measured sleep and glymphatic function across the Alzheimer's disease continuum. Better preserved slow-wave sleep and sleep oscillatory coupling were generally associated with more favorable brain clearance biomarkers, while disrupted sleep architecture was linked to impaired glymphatic clearance.

papers.title: Longitudinal Changes in Pictorial Declarative Memory After Six Months of Clinical Management in Adults with Suspected Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 265 patients with suspected obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) found that after six months of clinical management, immediate and delayed pictorial declarative memory improved, particularly in severe OSA. Baseline memory and indices of hypoxia and sleep fragmentation predicted memory changes, suggesting routine OSA management benefits declarative memory.

papers.title: Prunella vulgaris Compound Improves Sleep Architecture and Attenuates Hippocampal Injury in Insomnia Mice.
papers.summary: This study evaluated a Prunella vulgaris compound (PVC) in PCPA-induced insomnia mice. PVC shortened sleep latency, increased NREM and REM sleep, improved sleep continuity, attenuated hippocampal injury, modulated neurotransmitters (5-HT, GABA, glutamate, dopamine), and reduced NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptotic signaling.

papers.title: Chiropractic Care Is Associated with Frequency-Specific Reorganisation of Triple-Network Brain Dynamics: A Source-Localised EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a randomized secondary analysis of 76 adults with chronic low back pain, chiropractic care plus usual care was associated with increased resting-state alpha-band connectivity within the default mode network immediately post-intervention and at four-week follow-up compared to usual care alone, along with other frequency- and network-specific effects. Findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmatory pre-registered trials.

papers.title: Association Between Glucocorticoid Exposure and Objective Sleep Architecture in Rheumatoid Arthritis: An Exploratory Pilot EEG Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory pilot study of 20 rheumatoid arthritis patients compared objective sleep architecture between glucocorticoid users and non-users using EEG and accelerometry. Glucocorticoid users had longer wake after sleep onset, shorter NREM stage N3 duration, and lower delta power despite comparable disease activity, suggesting an association with poorer sleep continuity and reduced deep sleep.

papers.title: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) Augments Semiology in Stereotactic Electroencephalography (SEEG) Evaluations.
papers.summary: This review discusses the complementary role of magnetoencephalography (MEG) in presurgical epilepsy evaluations, particularly in developing stereotactic electroencephalography (SEEG) implantation strategies. It illustrates with two cases and reviews outcomes from evaluations incorporating MEG, concluding that MEG augments semiology in SEEG planning.

papers.title: Perioperative Airway Management in Treacher Collins Syndrome With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Case Report.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes perioperative airway management in a 28-year-old man with Treacher Collins syndrome and mild OSA undergoing orthognathic surgery. Using videolaryngoscopy-guided nasotracheal intubation and a structured multidisciplinary plan, the airway was successfully managed, and postoperative CBCT showed upper airway expansion.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Social Media Addiction, and Associated Factors in Children After Natural Disasters.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 369 middle school students found that social media addiction and sleep deprivation were significantly correlated, and using social media for disaster-related information was a key contributor to sleep deprivation. Disaster awareness education and preparedness activities were associated with lower levels of both.

papers.title: BMAL1-Mediated Circadian Regulation of Oocyte Quality and IVF Outcomes.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that circadian regulatory systems, particularly BMAL1, influence oocyte competence through mitochondrial activity, oxidative balance, meiosis, and metabolism. Dysregulated BMAL1 signaling is associated with compromised folliculogenesis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and reduced oocyte quality, potentially affecting assisted reproduction outcomes.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
